headline: Ranked LSU hosts struggling USC in defensive showcase
subhead: A ranked Tiger defense faces a Trojan offense searching for answers after Notre Dame's dominant win.

xFactor.why: LSU's defensive unit held Tennessee to just seven points and should similarly stifle USC's inconsistent offensive line and struggling receivers.

keyMatchup: LSU's defensive line pressure versus USC's already-thin pass protection will determine whether the Trojans can move the ball at all in the second half.
body: USC comes to Baton Rouge in disarray after Notre Dame dismantled them 28-16, exposing a offense that cannot execute in hostile environments. The Trojans' fourth-quarter collapse revealed depth issues at receiver and a rushing attack that disappeared when it mattered most. LSU, sitting at 7-4 and ranked sixth, enters with momentum from holding Tennessee scoreless in the second half—a statement win that showed their defensive coaching room has found a formula.

The real concern for USC is that LSU's front four will have all day to work. If the Trojan line fails to establish even a semblance of pocket presence, this becomes a long afternoon in Death Valley. LSU's recent defensive discipline, combined with home-field energy, gives the Tigers every advantage in a matchup where field position and turnover margin will likely determine the outcome.
